# Agent types (`agent-types/`)

An agent type (a "specialty") is a declarative bundle that says what a new agent
starts with: identity templates, system crons, plugins, tools, env contract and
feature flags. The `agent-types/` directory holds the type definitions and the JSON
schema they validate against.

```
agent-types/
├── specialty.schema.json        # generated JSON Schema for manifest.yaml
└── <type>/
    ├── manifest.yaml            # the Specialty manifest
    └── templates/               # workspace seed files (*.template)
```

Today the directory ships one type, `specialist`.

## Manifest

`manifest.yaml` is `apiVersion: shipwright.dev/v1alpha1`, `kind: Specialty`. It is
parsed and validated by `parseSpecialtyManifest()` in `admin/src/specialty-registry.ts`
(a Zod schema; unknown keys are rejected). Required top-level keys: `metadata`,
`identity`, `crons`, `plugins`, `tools`, `env`, `members`, `repos`, `chat`, `voice`.
`resources` (k8s-style `requests`/`limits` for cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage) is
optional.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `metadata` | `name` (DNS-label pattern, matches the directory), `displayName`, `description`, `version`, `skills[]` (`id`, `name`, `description`, `tags?`) |
| `identity.templatesDir` | Directory of workspace templates used to seed a new agent |
| `crons[]` | System crons: `name`, `schedule`, `prompt`, optional `preCheck`, `silent` (default false), `enabled` (default true), `parentCron` |
| `plugins`, `tools` | Plugins to install and allowed tool names |
| `env.required` / `env.optional` | `{key, description, secret}` entries describing the env contract |
| `members`, `repos` | Default members and repos |
| `chat`, `voice` | Feature flags |

The schema file is generated from the Zod source (`buildSpecialtyJsonSchema()`), never
hand-edited. `admin/src/specialty-registry.schema.unit.test.ts` deep-compares the
committed file with the regenerated one, so changing the Zod schema means updating
`specialty.schema.json` to match. The generator script that comments in the code refer
to (`scripts/generate-specialty-schema.ts`) does not exist in this repo yet, so there is
no regenerate command: the test only calls `buildSpecialtyJsonSchema()`, and the file has
to be updated by hand from its output. For field-level detail read the
schema rather than this doc.

## Templates

Seeded into a new agent's workspace by `resolveTemplatesDir()` in `runtime/setup.ts`.
Required: `CLAUDE.md.template`, `SOUL.md.template`, `IDENTITY.md.template`. A
type whose `templatesDir` is missing, unparseable or lacks one of these falls back to
the built-in `workspace/` directory with a warning; it never fails boot.
`SPECIALTY.md.template` is optional. Any other file (VOICE, mise, requirements,
BOOTSTRAP) falls back per file to the built-in `workspace/` directory.

`templatesDir` is resolved against the repo root first, then against the manifest's
own directory (for self-contained types).

## Resolution at runtime

`admin/src/specialty-manifest-loader.ts` maps an agent's stored `typeName` to its
manifest by reading `<specialties dir>/<typeName>/manifest.yaml`.

- `SHIPWRIGHT_SPECIALTIES_DIR` overrides the specialties directory.
- `SHIPWRIGHT_DEFAULT_AGENT_TYPE` overrides the fallback type (default `coding`).
- An unknown `typeName` falls back to the default type with a warning, so the
  cron reconcile route keeps working for renamed or removed types.
- If the default type itself fails to load or validate, the error propagates; it is a
  configuration error and is never degraded into "no crons".

## The `specialist` type

A generic, non-coding agent: no system crons, no plugins, no GitHub scope, tools
`Bash`, `WebSearch`, `WebFetch`, `Agent`, with `chat` and `voice` on. Its only required
env is `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; Slack, Groq/ElevenLabs/Whisper/Piper voice and
`GH_TOKEN` are optional. It is meant to be specialized after creation through the
admin API.

## Known drift

The `specialist` manifest and some loader comments still spell paths as
`specialties/specialist/...` (the monorepo layout), while the files live under
`agent-types/`. The loader's built-in default directory is likewise `<repo>/specialties`,
so in this repository point `SHIPWRIGHT_SPECIALTIES_DIR` at `agent-types/`.

That alone does not make the specialist templates load. The manifest's
`identity.templatesDir` is `specialties/specialist/templates/`, and `resolveTemplatesDir()`
tries it against the repo root and then against the manifest's own directory. Neither path
exists here, so the lookup throws, warns, and falls back to the built-in `workspace/`
templates. For the type to seed its own identity files, change the manifest's
`templatesDir` to `agent-types/specialist/templates/`.

## Adding a type

1. Create `agent-types/<name>/manifest.yaml` with `metadata.name` equal to `<name>`.
2. Add `templates/` with the three required templates.
3. Run the schema unit test and `bun run check:boundary`; the directory is scanned
   for imports that leave the repo.
